title: kbmon live view: ANSI redraw in place on macOS, Linux and Windows, plain frames on a pipe or NO_COLOR
goal: kbmon.py on a terminal or with --ansi redraws the panels in place every --interval seconds (1 to 300, default 5) with the ANSI cursor-home and erase sequences, cut to the terminal width, until Ctrl-C or --count frames and exits 0; on Windows mon_view.enable_vt() turns on the console's virtual terminal processing and kbmon writes plain frames when it returns False; NO_COLOR or a standard output that is no terminal gives frames with no escape byte unless --ansi; an --interval outside 1 to 300 or a --count below 1 exits 2

clauses.clause: kbmon.py on a terminal or with --ansi redraws the panels in place every --interval seconds (1 to 300, default 5) with the ANSI cursor-home and erase sequences, cut to the terminal width, until Ctrl-C or --count frames and exits 0
on Windows mon_view.enable_vt() turns on the console's virtual terminal processing and kbmon writes plain frames when it returns False
NO_COLOR or a standard output that is no terminal gives frames with no escape byte unless --ansi
an --interval outside 1 to 300 or a --count below 1 exits 2

gates.question: What does kbmon do on a Windows console where virtual terminal processing cannot be turned on?

ask: Does the Windows console honour ANSI escape sequences from Python print, or must virtual terminal processing be enabled with SetConsoleMode?
Which ANSI escape sequences clear the screen and move the cursor to the top left?

notes: Plan 2026-10-18: curses is not on Windows, so the view is ANSI with ctypes for the console mode. No host of this project runs the Windows console in a check: the planted enable_vt() case and the review stand in for it.
